G000565.title: House censured Gosar over animated video
G000565.summary: The House adopted H.Res. 789 censuring Gosar by a vote of 223 to 207, with one member voting present. The resolution followed his posting of an edited anime video depicting his likeness attacking Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and President Joe Biden.

sources.name: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House

S001150.title: House censured Schiff over Trump investigations
S001150.summary: The House voted 213 to 209, with six members voting present, to censure Schiff over his role in congressional investigations of President Donald Trump. The resolution accused him of misleading the public; Schiff called the allegations defamatory.

T000481.title: House censured Tlaib over Israel-Hamas war remarks
T000481.summary: The House voted 234 to 188 to censure Tlaib over her comments about the Israel-Hamas war, including her use of the phrase "from the river to the sea." An earlier censure resolution against her had been rejected.

T000481.title: Ethics committee directed campaign repayment
T000481.summary: The House Ethics Committee found that Tlaib accepted $10,800 in campaign-funded salary payments after her 2018 general election victory, when she was no longer a candidate, and directed her to reimburse her campaign committee. Her office said she hoped the FEC would clarify the rule.

G000553.title: House censured Green for disrupting presidential address
G000553.summary: The House voted 224 to 198 to censure Green after he stood and shouted during President Donald Trump's March 4, 2025, address to a joint session of Congress and was removed from the chamber. Ten Democrats voted for the resolution.

G000553.title: Former staffer's 2008 allegation withdrawn
G000553.summary: In 2008 former staffer Lucinda Daniels accused Green of sexual assault and later withdrew the allegation; Green had filed a counter-lawsuit alleging she threatened to sue him unless paid. In a November 2017 joint statement, both said the matter was resolved without payment by either side.

E000246.title: House censured Edwards after ethics report
E000246.summary: The House voted 413 to 2 to censure Edwards, as recommended by the Ethics Committee. The committee's August 3, 2026, report found he engaged in persistent inappropriate conduct toward two young female staffers in violation of the Code of Official Conduct, and found no evidence of sexual activity or explicit propositions. Edwards denied harassing the staffers and ended his reelection bid.

G000589.title: Ethics committee continuing review of travel and campaign spending
G000589.summary: The Office of Congressional Conduct referred allegations that Gooden sought official reimbursement for travel that may not have been for official purposes and that his campaign may have misreported disbursements not attributable to campaign purposes. The Ethics Committee published the referral and said it would continue its review, noting the review does not itself indicate a violation. Gooden denied the allegations.

G000585.title: Ethics committee reviewing sexual misconduct allegations
G000585.summary: The House Ethics Committee announced it is reviewing allegations that Gomez may have engaged in sexual misconduct, including inappropriate sexual contact with a House staffer, noting the review does not itself indicate a violation. Gomez said he made personal mistakes outside his marriage that were consensual and did not violate the law or House rules.

M001222.title: Judge dismissed defamation suit against former wife
M001222.summary: An Ohio judge dismissed Miller's defamation lawsuit against his former wife, Emily Moreno, concluding that her allegation that he doused her with hot water was "substantially true." Moreno's court filings also allege other physical abuse, which Miller denies.

M001222.title: Ethics committee reviewing domestic violence allegations
M001222.summary: The House Ethics Committee announced it is reviewing allegations that Miller may have engaged in domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use, noting the review does not itself indicate a violation. Miller, who had asked for an inquiry, denies the allegations.

M001216.title: Ethics subcommittee investigating multiple allegations
M001216.summary: The House Ethics Committee established an investigative subcommittee to examine allegations that Mills failed to properly disclose required financial information, violated campaign finance laws in his 2022 and 2024 campaigns, improperly accepted gifts, received special favors, engaged in sexual misconduct or dating violence, and misused congressional resources. In May 2026 the committee said the review includes a February 2025 incident in which D.C. police did not charge Mills after an assault report, and an October 2025 court-issued injunction limiting his contact with a woman. As of May 2026 the investigation was ongoing.

M000194.title: Ethics committee continuing review of lodging reimbursements
M000194.summary: The Office of Congressional Conduct board found substantial reason to believe Mace sought official reimbursements for lodging in 2023 and 2024 that did not reflect her actual incurred expenses. The Ethics Committee published the referral and Mace's response and said it would continue its review, noting the review does not itself indicate a violation.

C001129.title: Ethics committee continuing review of office payroll
C001129.summary: The Office of Congressional Conduct board found substantial reason to believe Collins used congressional resources for unauthorized purposes, citing allegations that a person paid as a district intern, who had a personal relationship with his chief of staff, did not perform work for the office. The Ethics Committee published the referral and Collins's response and said it would continue its review, noting the review does not itself indicate a violation.

O000172.title: Ethics committee found Met Gala gift violations
O000172.summary: The House Ethics Committee found that Ocasio-Cortez accepted impermissible gifts connected to the 2021 Met Gala, including free admission for her partner and items for which she did not pay full market value, and delayed appropriate payment. It found the violations were not knowing and willful, and said the matter would close upon repayment of the value of the gifts.

K000376.title: Ethics committee reproved Kelly over spouse's stock matter
K000376.summary: Reviewing a referral about his wife's 2020 purchase of Cleveland-Cliffs stock, the House Ethics Committee did not find evidence that Kelly knowingly caused her to trade on insider information, and could not determine whether the purchase was improper because she did not fully cooperate. It found he violated the Code of Official Conduct in his response to the investigation, including untimely disclosure of an additional purchase, issued a report serving as a reproval, and said the couple should divest before he takes further official action related to the company.

C001063.title: Pardoned after federal bribery indictment
C001063.summary: In May 2024 Cuellar and his wife were indicted on charges including bribery conspiracy, acting as agents of a foreign principal and money laundering; prosecutors alleged they accepted nearly $600,000 from an Azerbaijani-controlled company and a Mexican bank. Both said they were innocent. President Donald Trump pardoned the couple on December 3, 2025, before their scheduled trial.

C001063.title: Ethics subcommittee reauthorized after indictment
C001063.summary: After the 2024 indictment, the House Ethics Committee established an investigative subcommittee to examine whether Cuellar solicited or accepted bribes, acted as a foreign agent, violated money laundering laws, misused his position or made false disclosure statements. It reauthorized the subcommittee for the 119th Congress in July 2025; no later public action has been announced.

M001229.title: Federal assault charges pending after appeals ruling
M001229.summary: McIver was indicted in June 2025 on federal charges of assaulting, resisting or impeding immigration officers during a May 2025 oversight visit to the Delaney Hall detention center in Newark; she pleaded not guilty and has called the prosecution political intimidation. In August 2026 a federal appeals court ruled she is not immune from prosecution on two of the three counts and returned the third to the trial court. As of August 2026 the case was pending.

O000175.title: Ethics committee continuing review of campaign loan reports
O000175.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics board found substantial reason to believe Ogles misrepresented the amount he loaned his campaign, which had reported a $320,000 loan. The Ethics Committee published the referral and said it would continue its review. In August 2024 Ogles said FBI agents had seized his phone as part of an investigation into his campaign finances.

M001157.title: Public intoxication charge dismissed
M001157.summary: McCaul was charged in November 2024 with misdemeanor public intoxication at Washington Dulles International Airport; the charge was voluntarily dismissed on December 13, 2024. The House Ethics Committee voted not to open an investigative subcommittee and closed the matter.

S000929.title: Airport weapon charge dismissed
S000929.summary: Spartz was cited in June 2024 for carrying an unloaded handgun through security at Washington Dulles International Airport and charged with a misdemeanor; the charge was dismissed after she completed a gun safety course. She paid a TSA civil penalty, and the House Ethics Committee closed the matter without an investigative subcommittee.

H001058.title: Ethics committee closed campaign spending review
H001058.summary: The House Ethics Committee found that Huizenga and his staff generally acted within the law in spending campaign and official funds, though his campaign did not fully comply with reporting and reimbursement standards. It determined no sanction was merited and closed the matter with a report and a private letter.

H001095.title: Ethics committee closed campaign-funds review
H001095.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics referred allegations that Hunt may have converted campaign funds to personal use through a private club membership. In December 2024 the Ethics Committee closed the matter, saying that in the matters it resolved there was evidence of incomplete compliance with campaign-funds standards but no evidence any member intentionally misused funds.

J000304.title: Ethics committee closed campaign-funds review
J000304.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics referred allegations that Jackson may have converted campaign funds to personal use through a private club membership. In December 2024 the Ethics Committee closed the matter, saying that in the matters it resolved there was evidence of incomplete compliance with campaign-funds standards but no evidence any member intentionally misused funds.

J000304.title: Pentagon inspector general report on White House tenure
J000304.summary: A Defense Department inspector general report found that, as a White House physician, Jackson made sexual and denigrating statements about a female subordinate, mistreated subordinates and engaged in inappropriate conduct involving alcohol on two presidential trips. Jackson denied the allegations and called the report politically motivated.

B000490.title: Ethics committee closed campaign-funds review
B000490.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics had referred allegations that Bishop used campaign funds for personal expenses. In December 2024 the Ethics Committee closed the matter, saying that in the matters it resolved there was evidence of incomplete compliance with campaign-funds standards but no evidence any member intentionally misused funds.

N000026.title: Ethics committee reviewing campaign-funds referral
N000026.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics board found probable cause to believe Nehls may have converted campaign funds to personal use and omitted information from his financial disclosure statements. The Ethics Committee published the referral and Nehls's response and said it would continue its review; no later public action has been announced.

C000127.title: FEC admonished campaign over late loan disclosure
C000127.summary: The Federal Election Commission found no reason to believe that two bank credit lines to Cantwell's 2000 Senate campaign were improper corporate contributions, but found reason to believe the campaign failed to timely report complete loan information. The FEC sent an admonishment letter and took no other action.

B001277.title: Statements about Vietnam-era service
B001277.summary: The New York Times reported that Blumenthal, who served in the Marine Corps Reserve and did not deploy to Vietnam, had on occasion described himself as having served in Vietnam. Blumenthal said he had misspoken and later apologized for not being "clear or precise" about his service.

W000187.title: Ethics committee cleared Waters in OneUnited Bank case
W000187.summary: In 2010 a House ethics panel prepared charges over Waters' 2008 efforts on behalf of OneUnited Bank, in which her husband held stock. In September 2012 the committee, relying on an outside counsel's review, found no evidence that Waters knowingly violated House rules.

M001184.title: Fined under House mask rule; challenge dismissed
M001184.summary: Massie was fined $500 in May 2021 for not complying with the House floor mask requirement. He and two other members sued over the fines; the D.C. Circuit held the claims barred by the Speech or Debate Clause, and in February 2024 the Supreme Court declined to hear the case.

O000173.title: Home searched in federal criminal investigation
O000173.summary: Federal agents searched Omar's Washington home as part of a criminal investigation by Homeland Security Investigations, the Justice Department and the U.S. attorney in Minneapolis that, according to people familiar with it, deals partly with alleged immigration fraud; a magistrate judge limited how prosecutors could access her documents. Omar called the search the latest escalation in a campaign of political intimidation. As of October 2026, the investigation was ongoing.

O000173.title: State board ordered repayment of campaign funds
O000173.summary: Following a Minnesota Campaign Finance Board investigation into allegations that Omar misused campaign funds, she agreed to repay $3,500 and pay a $500 fine. Her campaign said her tax filings, which drew questions during the review, were fully compliant with tax law.

A000372.title: Reported STOCK Act disclosure lapses
A000372.summary: A Business Insider analysis found that Allen appeared to have improperly disclosed stock transactions, including seven holdings worth up to $140,000 that left his annual disclosure without transaction reports, and that he was about 15 months late reporting a June 2020 stock purchase by his wife. His office did not respond to inquiries.

B001291.title: Paid FEC civil penalty over 1996 campaign contributions
B001291.summary: According to the Federal Election Commission, Babin and his congressional campaign committee paid a $20,000 civil penalty and paid $5,000 in excessive contributions to the U.S. Treasury for accepting an excessive contribution and a contribution in the name of another and failing to disclose financial activity properly. The matter stemmed from 1996 donations by businessman Peter Cloeren, who pleaded guilty to campaign-finance violations.

S000250.title: Reported late disclosure of stock trades
S000250.summary: Business Insider reported that Sessions appeared to have violated the STOCK Act by not properly reporting seven of his own 2021 stock trades, valued between $7,001 and $105,000, the most overdue by four months.

M001212.title: Acquitted of perjury and false-statement charges
M001212.summary: In April 2014, while an Alabama state representative, Moore was arrested on felony charges of perjury and providing false statements to a special grand jury investigating public corruption. A jury found him not guilty in October 2014.

W000788.title: Charges dismissed after arrest at Georgia Capitol
W000788.summary: Williams, then a state senator, was arrested along with 14 protesters at the Georgia State Capitol during a protest over vote counting in the 2018 governor's race. The cases against all 15 were dismissed in June 2019.

M001213.title: Paid late-filing fee for stock trade disclosures
M001213.summary: Moore was weeks or months late in disclosing more than 70 stock and stock-option trades made between January and May 2021, worth an estimated $70,000 to $1.1 million, as required by the STOCK Act. His office said he worked with the Ethics Committee and paid a late filing fee in full.

W000790.title: Obstruction charge dismissed
W000790.summary: In 2002 Warnock, then a Baltimore pastor, and another minister were charged with interfering with police interviews of counselors in a child-abuse investigation at a church-run camp; Warnock said he had asserted that lawyers should be present. A judge dismissed the charges at the prosecutor's request; the prosecutor cited a miscommunication and said the ministers had been helpful to the investigation.

L000601.title: Open Meetings Act lawsuit settled; no criminal charges
L000601.summary: Landsman was one of five Cincinnati council members sued over private text messages about city business. Under a settlement approved in March 2019, the city admitted the members had violated Ohio's Open Meetings Act and the texts were released. In September 2020 a special prosecutor declined to bring criminal charges against the five.

B001324.title: County settled discrimination suit over Bell's tenure
B001324.summary: A former assistant prosecutor sued St. Louis County in 2020 alleging that Bell, then prosecuting attorney, discriminated against her based on gender, age and race and retaliated against her. In January 2025 the county agreed to pay $500,000 to settle the claims.

M001236.title: Alienation-of-affection lawsuit settled
M001236.summary: In June 2023 a Wake County man sued Moore, then North Carolina House speaker, for alienation of affection over Moore's relationship with his wife; the suit also alleged Moore used his political power in connection with the relationship, which Moore denied. The lawsuit was settled in July 2023 on undisclosed terms.

M001236.title: Stock trades disclosed after STOCK Act deadline
M001236.summary: Fortune reported that Moore disclosed several personal stock purchases made in April 2025 after the STOCK Act's 45-day deadline. Moore said the trades were disclosed within a 30-day grace period for technical delays recognized by the House Ethics Committee and that no late fee was assessed.

elect-MI7.title: Pleaded guilty after pipeline protest; conviction expunged
elect-MI7.summary: Lawrence was arrested in 2013 after he and other protesters attached themselves to construction equipment at an Enbridge pipeline site in Ingham County, Michigan. Charged with misdemeanor trespassing and felony resisting and obstructing a police officer, he pleaded guilty and was ordered to pay fines and serve probation; the conviction was later expunged.

C001035.title: FBI review of Navatek donations found nothing implicating Collins
C001035.summary: In September 2026, ProPublica reported that the FBI had examined claims tied to defense contractor Navatek, whose former chief executive Martin Kao was sentenced in 2025 to 33 months in prison over illegal straw donations to Collins's campaign and a super PAC supporting her. An FBI spokesperson said the agency had investigated the claims years earlier and "ultimately found nothing implicating Senator Collins or Senator Collins' campaign." Collins's office said it fully cooperated and that the matter was resolved when the campaign disgorged the illegal contributions.

B001260.title: Ethics committee cleared financial disclosure errors
B001260.summary: The House Ethics Committee cleared Buchanan of allegations that he violated House rules by intentionally misleading Congress in his financial disclosure forms. The committee said it found no evidence the errors were knowing or willful, and Buchanan amended his disclosures.

B001260.title: Campaign contribution inquiries closed without action
B001260.summary: Buchanan was investigated by the House Ethics Committee, the Office of Congressional Ethics, the FEC and the Justice Department over allegations that car dealerships he partly owned illegally reimbursed employees for contributions to his campaign and that he tried to influence a former business partner's testimony to the FEC. In September 2012 his attorneys said the Justice Department had closed its investigation without charges, and the FEC fined other individuals and companies but not Buchanan or his campaign. In June 2016 the Ethics Committee closed its review, citing insufficient evidence.

C001080.title: Ethics committee issued letter of reproval
C001080.summary: The House Ethics Committee found that Chu's chief of staff and legislative director had directed staff to do campaign work using official resources, and found no evidence that Chu was aware of it. The committee found that emails Chu sent to staff interfered with its investigation and issued her a public letter of reproval.

D000616.title: State medical board fined him over relationships with patients
D000616.summary: The Tennessee Board of Medical Examiners fined DesJarlais, a licensed physician, $500 for sexual relationships with two female patients; he was also required to pay $1,000 toward the cost of the board's investigation.

M001153.title: Senate ethics complaint over land purchase
M001153.summary: A watchdog group filed a Senate ethics complaint alleging that Murkowski bought Kenai River property from businessman Bob Penney below market value. Murkowski said the deal was proper and sold the land back to Penney for the $179,400 purchase price; nothing came of the complaint, and in 2008 she revised her financial disclosures going back to 2004.

P000603.title: Disclosed spouse's Gilead stock purchase 16 months late
P000603.summary: Paul disclosed in August 2021 that his wife bought between $1,001 and $15,000 of Gilead Sciences stock on February 26, 2020, more than 16 months after the STOCK Act deadline for reporting it. Paul said the disclosure had been prepared but was not transmitted.

M001199.title: Late STOCK Act disclosures of stock trades
M001199.summary: Business Insider reported that Mast disclosed July 2021 purchases of up to $100,000 in Virgin Galactic stock after the STOCK Act deadline, and that a February 2021 sale of up to $50,000 in Ideal Power stock was not reported until August 2022. His office said the Ideal Power transaction was missed due to an administrative error.

G000583.title: Late STOCK Act stock-trade disclosure
G000583.summary: Business Insider reported in August 2022 that Gottheimer violated the STOCK Act's 45-day reporting requirement with a late stock-trade disclosure. Gottheimer said he was in the process of placing his assets in a blind trust.

N000190.title: Fined under House mask rule; challenge dismissed
N000190.summary: Norman was one of three House members fined $500 in May 2021 for not wearing a mask on the House floor in violation of the chamber's rule. Their lawsuit challenging the fines was dismissed under the Speech or Debate Clause, a federal appeals court affirmed in June 2023, and the Supreme Court declined to hear the case in February 2024.

C001116.title: Fined for bypassing House metal detectors; challenge dismissed
C001116.summary: Clyde was fined for not complying with security screening at the House chamber entrance put in place after the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack; his appeal to the House Ethics Committee was denied and the fines were deducted from his salary. A federal judge dismissed his lawsuit over the fines in August 2022, an appeals panel upheld that ruling, and the Supreme Court declined to hear the case in April 2024.

T000278.title: Late disclosure of 132 stock trades
T000278.summary: Business Insider reported that Tuberville disclosed 132 stock trades made in 2021, totaling at least $894,000, weeks or months after the STOCK Act deadline. A spokeswoman said financial advisers handled his trading and that he had not known about the individual trades.

T000278.title: Settled investor lawsuit over hedge fund
T000278.summary: Investors sued Tuberville and his business partner John David Stroud in 2012, alleging that their hedge fund TS Capital defrauded them of more than $1.7 million; Tuberville's attorneys denied the allegations. A federal judge approved a settlement in October 2013 on undisclosed terms. Stroud pleaded guilty to securities fraud, and Tuberville was not charged.

P000610.title: Epstein-related lawsuit dismissed with prejudice
P000610.summary: Women identified as Jane Does sued Plaskett and other U.S. Virgin Islands officials in November 2023, alleging they helped and benefited from Jeffrey Epstein's sex-trafficking enterprise; Plaskett sought dismissal. In August 2025 the parties filed a stipulation dismissing the claims against her with prejudice.

elect-NY10.title: Apologized for ethics violation over nonprofit solicitation
elect-NY10.summary: As a New York City Council member, Lander sent an email from his official account urging recipients to donate to Local Progress, a nonprofit he helped create and chaired. He apologized days later for violating ethics rules.

elect-NY10.title: Found not guilty after immigration court arrest
elect-NY10.summary: Lander was detained at 26 Federal Plaza in June and September 2025 while seeking access to ICE holding areas; charges from the June incident were dropped. After the September arrest he was cited for allegedly blocking an elevator, and in June 2026 a federal judge found him not guilty in a bench trial.

S001232.title: Acknowledged false statement to park ranger about gunshot wound
S001232.summary: Sheehy was ticketed in 2015 and paid a $525 fine for illegally discharging a firearm in Glacier National Park after telling a ranger his gun fell and fired. In April 2024 he said he had lied to the ranger and that the wound came from Afghanistan in 2012; the former ranger said in October 2024 that Sheehy had shot himself at Glacier, which Sheehy's campaign called a defamatory story.

S001232.title: Former employees' breach-of-contract lawsuit
S001232.summary: Two former employees sued Sheehy and his brother alleging breach of contract over their shares in the company structure behind Ascent Vision Technologies; the Sheehys denied the allegations. As of October 2024, the case was pending, and the plaintiffs alleged in a court filing that an operating agreement the Sheehys submitted had been altered.

elect-NY21.title: Defendant in two defamation lawsuits
elect-NY21.summary: Constantino was sued for defamation by state Conservative Party chair Gerard Kassar over Constantino's claim that Kassar threatened to kill him, and separately by Philip Perry, fiance of the Clinton County Republican chair, over social media posts. As of October 2026, both lawsuits were pending.

J000312.title: Senate ethics committee issued public letter of admonition
J000312.summary: The Senate Select Committee on Ethics issued Justice a public letter of admonition concerning the timeliness of his financial disclosure. The committee wrote that his actions resulted in harm to public trust in the Senate and a violation of federal law.

J000312.title: Residency lawsuit resolved with agreement to live in Charleston
J000312.summary: A former state lawmaker sued Justice in 2018 alleging that, as governor, he did not reside at the seat of government in Charleston as the West Virginia Constitution requires. In March 2021 Justice agreed to reside in Charleston and a judge dismissed the suit.

C001061.title: Bank lawsuit over car wash loan settled
C001061.summary: Bank of America sued Cleaver, his wife and Cleaver Co. LLC over delinquent loans used to buy a Grandview car wash; the parties settled in April 2013 just before trial, leaving the Cleavers responsible for more than $1.2 million in future payments. In 2014 a Jackson County court clerk issued an order to garnish Cleaver's congressional wages on the bank's behalf. Cleaver said in a statement that he and his wife would meet all of their legal obligations.

C000880.title: Pleaded guilty to drunk driving
C000880.summary: Crapo pleaded guilty in Alexandria District Court to drunk driving following a December 2012 arrest in Alexandria, Virginia. He was sentenced to 180 days in jail, all suspended, a one-year license suspension with eligibility for a restricted license, a $250 fine and an alcohol program, and issued a public apology.

G000546.title: Ethics committee found no violation in witness matter
G000546.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics referred Graves to the House ethics committee over his role in inviting Brooks Hurst, who held investments in two renewable fuel cooperatives alongside Graves' wife, to testify at a March 2009 Small Business Committee hearing. The committee concluded in October 2009 that Graves did not violate any House rule or standard of conduct and closed the matter.

sources.name: House Committee on Standards of Official Conduct (House Report 111-320)

S001183.title: Reprimanded by House after admitting 11 violations
S001183.summary: Following a House Ethics Committee investigation opened in 2018, Schweikert admitted to 11 violations, including campaign finance reporting violations, personal use of campaign funds, misuse of official funds and pressuring staff to do campaign work, and agreed to pay a $50,000 fine. The House formally reprimanded him by voice vote on July 31, 2020.

W000795.title: House passed resolution of disapproval over outburst
W000795.summary: After Wilson shouted "You lie!" during President Obama's September 2009 address to a joint session of Congress, the House voted 240-179 for a resolution of disapproval stating the outburst was a breach of decorum. Wilson had apologized after the speech but declined to apologize again on the House floor.

D000622.title: Workplace retaliation lawsuit settled
D000622.summary: Two Illinois Department of Veterans Affairs employees sued Duckworth, alleging workplace retaliation during her time as head of the department. The suit was settled in June 2016 for $26,000 paid by the state with no finding of wrongdoing; after the plaintiffs did not sign, a judge in August 2016 vacated the trial date and gave them 21 days to sign the agreement. Duckworth's campaign called it a frivolous workplace case.

W000816.title: Ethics committee took no action over auto dealer amendment
W000816.summary: The Office of Congressional Ethics voted 6-0 in 2016 to refer Williams to the House Ethics Committee over an amendment he offered that would have let car dealers rent or loan vehicles under safety recalls, finding substantial reason to believe his dealership interest may be perceived as having influenced his official duties; it said he did not cooperate with its review. In August 2017 the committee decided not to take action, finding no reasonable inference of improper conduct, but said Williams should have consulted it first. Williams said he knew he would be cleared.

W000816.title: Spouse's stock trades not properly reported
W000816.summary: Business Insider's January 2023 tally of STOCK Act disclosure violations listed Williams as not properly reporting three stock transactions his wife made in 2019, as reported by NPR citing Campaign Legal Center research.

C001101.title: Late disclosure of spouse's stock trades
C001101.summary: Clark disclosed on Aug. 15, 2021, 19 stock transactions by her husband made on June 4, valued between $19,019 and $285,000, past the STOCK Act's 45-day deadline, as first reported by Business Insider; a watchdog group filed a complaint with the Office of Congressional Ethics. Business Insider later reported she had stopped trading stocks.

R000606.title: Late disclosures of spouse's stock transactions
R000606.summary: Business Insider reported that Raskin did not disclose on three annual reports his wife's stock in Reserve Trust and disclosed her $1.5 million sale of it months late, a delay he attributed to his son's death. In June 2022 he disclosed about two months late a $250,001-$500,000 stock exchange his wife received in a merger, and said he paid a $200 late fee after consulting Ethics staff.

S001198.title: Late disclosure of two stock sales
S001198.summary: Sullivan reported on Nov. 3, 2022, two August stock sales, in Mowi and Five Below, past the STOCK Act's 45-day deadline. His disclosure said a third-party investment professional sold the inherited stocks and did not notify him until Oct. 30; a spokesman said the senator complies with all Senate ethics and disclosure requirements.

S001217.title: Late disclosure of stock sale
S001217.summary: Business Insider reported that Scott on Aug. 15, 2022, disclosed that he and his wife sold up to $450,000 in stock in Emida Corporation in September 2021, months after the federal reporting deadline.

K000377.title: Grand jury declined to indict over troops video
K000377.summary: After Kelly and five other Democratic lawmakers released a November 2025 video urging service members to refuse illegal orders, the Defense Department announced a review of what it called serious allegations of misconduct by Kelly, a retired Navy captain. In February 2026 a federal grand jury declined to indict Democratic lawmakers who appeared in the video, according to CNN; it was not immediately clear which lawmakers prosecutors sought to charge.

K000377.title: Court blocked Pentagon action on retirement grade
K000377.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth moved to censure Kelly and review his retirement grade over the video, which could reduce his rank and retirement pay; Kelly sued, alleging retaliation for protected speech. Judge Richard Leon granted a preliminary injunction on Feb. 12, 2026, and Hegseth said the ruling would be appealed. As of February 2026, the case was ongoing.

K000377.title: Late disclosure of stock option exercise
K000377.summary: Business Insider's January 2023 tally of STOCK Act disclosure violations listed Kelly as failing to disclose on time his exercise of a stock option on an investment in a company developing a supersonic passenger aircraft, as first reported by Fox Business.

H000273.title: State ethics commission fined him for gift ban violations
H000273.summary: Colorado's Independent Ethics Commission found that Hickenlooper violated the state constitution's gift ban while governor by accepting a private jet flight to Connecticut and a Maserati limousine ride at a conference in Italy, and ordered him to pay $2,750; it found three other flights did not violate the ban. The commission also held him in contempt for initially defying a subpoena to testify but imposed no penalty for it. His campaign said he accepted the findings and took responsibility.

H000273.title: Late disclosures of household stock trades in 2022
H000273.summary: Business Insider reported that Hickenlooper disclosed between two and 14 months late stock purchases by his wife worth $516,006 to $1.2 million and sales worth $130,004 to $300,000, after Sludge reported in May 2022 that he had been late disclosing five other household trades worth $565,000 to $1.3 million. He did not respond to Business Insider's questions.

H000273.title: Late disclosures of family stock sales in 2026
H000273.summary: NOTUS reported that on May 5, 2026, Hickenlooper reported nearly a year past the deadline his wife's sale of $500,000 to $1 million in Liberty Broadband stock, and was similarly late disclosing a sale of Palantir stock held by his dependent child. His office noted he co-sponsors a bill requiring members to use blind trusts.

B000825.title: Disorderly conduct charge dismissed
B000825.summary: Boebert was cited for misdemeanor disorderly conduct after an altercation with deputies at a music festival in June 2015, and was arrested in December 2015 for failing to appear in court. The charge was dismissed the following month after a prosecutor wrote there was no reasonable likelihood of conviction at trial.

B000825.title: Pleaded guilty to traffic charge after failure to appear
B000825.summary: After a 2016 crash, Boebert was charged with careless driving and operating an unsafe vehicle; she was booked into the Garfield County Jail on Feb. 13, 2017, for failing to appear in court. She later pleaded guilty to the unsafe vehicle charge and the careless driving charge was dropped.

B000825.title: Belatedly disclosed husband's consulting income
B000825.summary: Boebert disclosed in August 2021 that her husband earned $478,000 in 2020 and $460,000 in 2019 as a consultant for an energy firm, income she had not identified on her earlier candidate disclosure. The same day, the Federal Election Commission asked her campaign for information about Venmo payments totaling more than $6,000.

B000825.title: Late disclosure of spouse's 2021 transactions
B000825.summary: Business Insider's January 2023 tally of STOCK Act disclosure violations listed Boebert as failing for months to disclose $5,000 to $80,000 in 2021 transactions involving stocks, cryptocurrency and brokerage funds belonging to her husband, as reported by The Colorado Sun.

Z000018.title: Inspector general reviewed charter flight
Z000018.summary: The Interior Department's inspector general found that ethics officials approved Zinke's $12,375 charter flight after a June 2017 speech to the Las Vegas Golden Knights without complete information, including that the event had no connection to the department, and that the charter might have been avoided with better planning.

Z000018.title: Inspector general found ethics violations in Whitefish matter
Z000018.summary: In a February 2022 report on a real estate arrangement in Whitefish, Montana, the Interior inspector general found ethical and other violations by Zinke as Interior secretary, including that he knowingly provided incorrect, incomplete and misleading answers to investigators. The Justice Department declined to pursue criminal charges.

Z000018.title: Inspector general found lack of candor in casino probe
Z000018.summary: The Interior inspector general found that Zinke and his chief of staff did not comply with their duty of candor in statements to investigators about the department's handling of a Connecticut tribal casino proposal. The Justice Department declined prosecution in 2021. Zinke's attorney called the report a political smear and said Zinke lacked jurisdiction over the application.

L000599.title: Pleaded guilty to impaired driving after 2012 arrest
L000599.summary: Lawler disclosed in July 2026 that he was arrested for drunk driving on St. Patrick's Day 2012 after failing a Breathalyzer test, and later pleaded guilty to the lesser offense of driving while ability impaired. He called it one of the worst decisions of his life.

S001226.title: Appeals court dismissed suit over campaign ad
S001226.summary: Salinas' 2022 opponent Mike Erickson sued her and her campaign committee under Oregon election law over an ad saying he was charged with felony drug possession. The Oregon Court of Appeals ruled in January 2025 that the statement was not shown to be false under the statute, reversing the trial court and directing that the complaint be dismissed.

R000619.title: Late disclosure of 22 stock trades
R000619.summary: NOTUS reported that Rulli disclosed 22 personal stock trades, including in Palantir and Pfizer, months after the STOCK Act's 45-day deadline. His office did not respond to questions, including whether he paid a fine.

M001242.title: Wage lawsuits ended in judgment and settlements
M001242.summary: In a wage lawsuit by former salespeople at his Massachusetts dealership, a jury found in August 2022 that two employees had proven unpaid overtime, and the judge ordered Moreno to pay $416,160; the judge also allowed jurors to consider that records Moreno acknowledged shredding were destroyed. Moreno settled 14 of 16 related lawsuits in January 2023.

L000607.title: Court found public records law violated
L000607.summary: San Jose Spotlight and the First Amendment Coalition sued Liccardo, then mayor, and the city in 2022 under the California Public Records Act. In August 2023 a Santa Clara County judge found the city and Liccardo violated the law by failing to adequately search his private texts and emails for public records, and the city prepared to pay $500,000 in attorneys' fees. Liccardo said taxpayers would be better served by an appeal.

S001156.title: Late disclosure of Cisco stock sale
S001156.summary: NOTUS reported that Sánchez disclosed after the STOCK Act's 45-day window a sale of up to $15,000 in Cisco stock. A spokesperson said the stock belonged to her teenage son, that she reported the sale to the Ethics Committee and filed an amended disclosure, and that no fine was required because it fell within a grace period.

M001245.title: Late disclosure of stock sales
M001245.summary: NOTUS reported that Menefee disclosed weeks late sales of Berkshire Hathaway and Pinterest stock worth $47,005 to $180,000. Menefee said he had left the reports in draft status by mistake, filed them and notified the Ethics Committee, and requested a waiver of the late fee, saying he would pay it if the waiver was denied.

W000802.title: Late disclosure of Target and Tesla stock purchases
W000802.summary: Business Insider reported that Whitehouse disclosed January 2022 purchases of Target and Tesla shares, each worth $15,000 to $50,000, after the STOCK Act's 45-day deadline. His office acknowledged the filing was two days late and attributed it to a staff transition.

C000537.title: Reported FBI bribery inquiry involving Navatek
C000537.summary: ProPublica reported that FBI agents investigating alleged pay-for-play by contractor Navatek were examining Clyburn's interactions with the company's former CEO, who told agents Clyburn asked for $100,000 in contributions; Clyburn was not designated a formal subject. According to ProPublica, the investigation ended after the agents left the FBI in 2025 and 2026, and no charges were filed. Clyburn's office said a donation would never cause him to increase his support for a donor's request.

P000597.title: FEC fine over 2010 private jet flights
P000597.summary: The Federal Election Commission released a conciliation agreement fining Pingree's campaign $9,750 and requiring repayment of more than $13,000 for two 2010 flights on a jet owned by her then-fiance that were linked to campaign events. Pingree said she disagreed with the FEC's view but settled the matter.

P000597.title: Late disclosure of Treasury securities purchases
P000597.summary: Pingree disclosed six February 2025 purchases of U.S. Treasury securities worth $90,000 to $300,000 after the STOCK Act deadline. She attributed the delay to a paperwork error, and her office said she paid the standard $200 late-filing penalty.

S001189.title: Late disclosure of spouse's stock transactions
S001189.summary: Business Insider reported that Scott was about a week late in reporting several stock transactions made by his spouse, as required under the STOCK Act.

J000289.title: Former wrestlers alleged he knew of team doctor's abuse
J000289.summary: Former Ohio State wrestlers alleged that Jordan, an assistant wrestling coach in the late 1980s and early 1990s, knew of sexual abuse by team physician Richard Strauss and did not report it. Jordan denied any knowledge; a spokesperson said he 'never saw or heard of any abuse, and if he had, he would have dealt with it.' Former head coach Russ Hellickson said he never discussed the doctor with Jordan.

S001201.title: Ethics committee dismissed stock-reporting referral
S001201.summary: After a Campaign Legal Center complaint alleging about 300 unreported transactions, the Office of Congressional Ethics referred Suozzi to the House Ethics Committee over late periodic transaction reports. The committee unanimously dismissed the referral in July 2022, finding the failures were not knowing or willful; Suozzi said any errors were unintentional.

R000609.title: Ethics committee dismissed late stock-report referral
R000609.summary: In February 2022 the Office of Congressional Ethics referred Rutherford to the House Ethics Committee, finding substantial reason to believe he failed to file timely periodic transaction reports; he had paid $800 in late penalties. On August 24, 2022, the committee unanimously dismissed the referral, concluding there was no clear evidence the errors were knowing or willful.

T000482.title: Ethics committee cleared campaign finance inquiry
T000482.summary: The House Ethics Committee reviewed allegations that Trahan's 2018 campaign accepted contributions above federal limits and failed to make proper disclosures. The committee voted unanimously to dismiss the inquiry, stating it did not find that Trahan violated House rules, laws or other standards of conduct.

C001098.title: FEC fine over undisclosed 2012 campaign loans
C001098.summary: The Federal Election Commission fined Cruz's 2012 Senate campaign $35,000 for failing to disclose that about $1.06 million of the money he lent the campaign came from loans by Goldman Sachs and Citibank. The fine followed a 2016 complaint by the Campaign Legal Center.

G000574.title: Senate Ethics Committee dismissed complaint
G000574.summary: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna filed a complaint with the Senate Ethics Committee in April 2026 alleging campaign finance violations and sexual misconduct by Gallego, who denied the allegations. In a June 26, 2026 letter, the committee dismissed the complaint, stating it did not find evidence that his actions violated federal law, Senate rules or related standards of conduct.

I000056.title: 1972 arrests and misdemeanor gun conviction
I000056.summary: Court records reviewed by the San Francisco Chronicle showed Issa was arrested in Ohio in March 1972 and indicted on a larceny charge involving a car theft; the weapons charge and then the theft charge were dropped. In December 1972 he was arrested in Michigan for possession of an unregistered handgun, pleaded guilty or no contest, and was fined $100 and placed on three months' probation.

D000032.title: Stock trades not reported in periodic filings
D000032.summary: Business Insider reported that Donalds and his wife made over 100 trades worth $108,000 to $1.6 million in 2022 and 2023 that were listed on annual disclosures but not on the periodic transaction reports required within 45 days. The Campaign Legal Center filed an ethics complaint over the filings.

D000032.title: Civil lawsuit alleges 2022 assault
D000032.summary: Collier County School Board member Kelly Mason filed a civil assault lawsuit alleging Donalds threatened and intimidated her during an August 2022 confrontation in a Naples grocery store. Donalds' campaign called the suit a baseless, politically motivated attack. As of July 2026, the case was pending.

T000488.title: Settled business fraud lawsuit over company sale
T000488.summary: The buyer of Thanedar's company Avomeen sued him alleging he inflated the company's value before its 2016 sale. Thanedar disputed wrongdoing and filed a counterclaim; the parties settled on undisclosed terms days before the scheduled August 2019 trial.

M001241.title: No contest plea to misdemeanor DUI
M001241.summary: Min, then a California state senator, was arrested in Sacramento in May 2023 for driving under the influence and apologized. He pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor DUI charge and was sentenced to two days in jail, a first-offender program and three years of informal probation.

D000634.title: Guilty pleas to hunting license misdemeanors
D000634.summary: Downing was cited in 2017 for buying resident hunting and fishing licenses while not a Montana resident. In July 2018 he pleaded guilty to two misdemeanors under a plea deal and was ordered to pay a $2,110 fine, forfeit Montana hunting, fishing and trapping licenses for 18 months, and serve a one-year deferred sentence.

M001244.title: Grand jury report on Hope Florida settlement
M001244.summary: A Florida state grand jury report, obtained by CBS News Miami, found that $10 million from a 2024 Medicaid settlement with Centene was misappropriated through the Hope Florida Foundation, and concluded that Moody, then attorney general, was aware of the plan and authorized her chief deputy to sign the settlement. The grand jury did not bring criminal charges, and Moody rejected allegations of wrongdoing.

V000134.title: Dismissed from defamation lawsuit
V000134.summary: As mayor of Irving, Van Duyne was named a defendant in a defamation lawsuit filed by the father of Ahmed Mohamed, the student detained in 2015 over a homemade clock. A Dallas County court dismissed her from the suit in January 2017 after the plaintiff agreed to remove her.

B001309.title: Defamation lawsuit over parade shooting posts dismissed
B001309.summary: Denton Loudermill Jr. sued Burchett in federal court in Kansas, alleging Burchett's social media posts falsely identified him as a shooter at the February 2024 Kansas City parade and as an 'illegal alien.' Burchett moved to dismiss, arguing the Kansas court lacked jurisdiction, and a federal judge dismissed the lawsuit in September 2024.

F000110.title: FBI videotape shown at Edwards corruption trial
F000110.summary: At the 2000 federal corruption trial of former Gov. Edwin Edwards, an FBI agent testified that a hidden camera recorded Fields, then a state senator, handling a wad of cash in Edwards' office in 1997. Prosecutors alleged Fields passed the money to another state senator in exchange for a confidential gambling report; Fields was not among the defendants on trial.

O000176.title: County inspector general found no improper benefits
O000176.summary: The Baltimore County inspector general investigated whether Olszewski's administration gave improper benefits to a retired county firefighter and awarded a trucking contract based on Olszewski's friendship with a company employee. The December 2024 report found no evidence of either.
